title: 1. Asset Valuations - Financial Stability Report - April 2024
summary: The Federal Reserve's April 2024 Financial Stability Report found that asset valuations increased to elevated levels relative to fundamentals, with equity valuations rising further and corporate credit spreads narrowing to the lower range of historical distributions. Treasury market liquidity remained low by historical standards, while residential real estate valuations stayed near mid-2000s peaks and commercial real estate conditions continued deteriorating, especially in the office sector.
key_points: Equity market valuations increased, with the S&P 500 price-to-earnings ratio rising to the upper end of its historical distribution since 1989
Corporate credit spreads narrowed to levels in the lower range of their historical distributions, indicating stretched valuations in corporate bond markets
Treasury market liquidity remained low by historical standards, though consistent with elevated interest rate volatility; term premium remained low relative to long-run history
Residential real estate valuations remained near peak levels seen in the mid-2000s
Commercial real estate prices declined year-over-year (-1.3% real growth Dec 2022-Dec 2023), with high vacancy rates and weakening rents, particularly in the office sector
Farmland prices were historically elevated relative to rents, reflecting limited inventories of land
why_it_matters: This Federal Reserve assessment provides a comprehensive snapshot of U.S. asset valuations and market conditions as of early 2024. The report flags stretched equity and corporate bond valuations alongside elevated real estate valuations, which inform systemic risk monitoring. Low Treasury market liquidity is explicitly noted as a potential amplifier of shocks to asset valuations, relevant for investors and policymakers tracking market resilience.
market_structure_context: Treasury market liquidity remained low by historical standards, consistent with elevated measures of interest rate volatility. The report notes that Treasury market conditions 'could amplify the impact of shocks on asset valuations.' Interest rate volatility, derived from swaption options, declined slightly but remained elevated by historical norms, reflecting uncertainty about the economic outlook and monetary policy path. Term premium estimates remained low relative to long-run history.
notes: Historical record from April 2024. Data extends through 2023:Q4. This is Section 1 of the Federal Reserve's Financial Stability Report, focusing specifically on asset valuations. The report provides important market structure context regarding liquidity conditions and valuation levels, but the data is approximately 2 years old and should be treated as historical reference. Market structure findings (low Treasury liquidity, stretched valuations) remain directionally relevant as benchmarks but may not reflect current conditions.
